topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture by connecting to histopathology practicals and setting out the learning outcomes.

topics.label: Tumor viruses, cellular oncogenes, and transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the discovery of transforming tumor viruses established that cancer arises from altered cellular proto-oncogenes and led to experimental assays for cell transformation.

topics.label: Classification and genetic mechanisms of oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes are defined, how they control cell cycle progression, and how different types of mutations alter their genetic behavior.

topics.label: Mechanisms and consequences of sequence and chromosomal instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the cellular defects in DNA repair, replication proofreading, and chromosome segregation that generate sequence and chromosomal instability in cancer cells.

topics.label: Multistep tumor progression and hereditary cancer predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer develops through the sequential accumulation of genetic alterations and how inherited germline mutations accelerate this progression.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with review, recommended reading, and a preview of the next session.
